subject: The 3-minute mistake 90% of users make
preview_text: I discovered why most people never see the real patterns. It's not the app. It's this one thing.
body_paragraphs: I need to confess something. For the first month after building this, I thought it wasn't working. The scans felt random. The patterns weren't clear. Then I realized I was using it wrong. I was waiting for the big, obvious red flags to appear.

The truth is, toxicity isn't a single explosion. It's a slow leak. It's the tiny comment on Tuesday. The weird text on Thursday. The 'joke' that didn't land on Saturday. If you only scan when you're already upset, you're only seeing the smoke. You're missing the fire. The real power comes from catching the embers before they ignite.

That's why the most effective users have one simple habit. Every Sunday night, they open the app for exactly 3 minutes. They scroll back through their week's messages. They scan 2-3 random, normal-seeming conversations. Not the fights. The boring ones. The 'how was your day' texts. That's where the real patterns live. The dashboard connects these dots across time, showing you the slow creep of manipulation you'd otherwise miss completely.

This Sunday, open the app. Don't scan the fight. Scan the Tuesday small talk. See what the AI finds in the mundane. It will change how you see everything. P.S. The users who do this weekly routine are 10x more likely to spot gaslighting before it takes root. They're the ones who message me saying 'you just saved me a year of pain.'
